Label distribution

R3 removes 67% of records; the phone only removes 59%. R3 is biased toward removal.

Kushal -> This graph can be used to show that R3 is more aligned towards the removing the record as center vaala bar is very high

Confusion matrix

The full 3x3 R3-vs-phone grid. The heavy off-diagonal cells are the accuracy gap.

Reliability by R3 label

R3 "keep" decisions are right only 38.7% of the time; "remove" decisions 69.5%. The keeps are the weak spot.

Confidence is inverted

R3 is LEAST accurate exactly where its web-confidence score is highest (score 100 -> 43%).

Geography

AL (6%), MI (25%), NJ (31%) collapse the average. NE / KY / WA exceed 88%.

Specialty

Hospital-affiliated physician specialties (Peds, Cardiology, OB/GYN, IM) agree only 2-5%.

Claims presence

Any claims activity nearly doubles R3 reliability (74% vs 38.6%). Cheapest passive signal.

Error direction

R3 over-removes: 465 false removals vs 276 missed-bad records.

Claim recency / staleness

Fresher claims track higher R3 reliability - a basis for a staleness score (Track 2).

Triage map

High confidence + no claims = 18% correct: the confidently-wrong danger zone to call first (Track 3).

Notes: "both-conclusive" = records where both R3 and Call QC returned ACCURATE/INACCURATE (n=1,973). Call QC treated as ground truth per problem statement. Production R3 accuracy is ~75%; this Base Data is a hard sample where R3 underperforms. HIPAA-adjacent data - kept local, no external uploads.
